# Jubilees Chapter 35 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Rebekah speaks her last; Esau reconciled to Jacob; Rebekah dies

---

**35:1** In the forty-fifth jubilee, seventh week, first year, Rebekah called Jacob to her bedside and spoke to him about his brother Esau.

**35:2** "I've watched Esau, son," she said. "I've paid attention. His behavior is wicked — a steady stream of evil. He doesn't listen to a word his father or I say.

**35:3** But you — watch yourself. Live with integrity. Do that and you'll find favor with God and with people.

**35:4** Be careful with Esau. Don't let him get the upper hand. Don't let quarrels start between you — brothers shedding each other's blood would be an abomination to God.

**35:5** Understand this: the children of Belial will rise against Israel, against all the nations.

**35:6** Esau worries me. He could hurt you. Stay alert around him. But don't plot against him.

**35:7** Jacob — I want you to know: from the moment you were in my womb, I have loved you with everything I have. More than any of my children. You are my beloved."

**35:8** She was crying. Jacob cried too.

**35:9** "LORD God," she prayed aloud, "please — don't let me live to see Jacob die before me. I couldn't bear it."

**35:10** Then she sent for Esau. When he came, she said: "I need to talk to you."

**35:11** "Will you listen to me, son?" He said, "Yes, Mother."

**35:12** "I'm asking you — I'm begging you — to honor your brother Jacob. Love him.

**35:13** I love both of you. But this one thing: don't harm him. Not now, not ever, for as long as you live. I could not bear being his enemy."

**35:14** Esau said, "I'll do it. I won't touch Jacob. I've already let it go — I love him more than I love myself."

**35:15** "Then thank God for giving you a heart that can reconcile," Rebekah said. "You've just said before the LORD that you won't harm Jacob. Now swear it to me. Swear by God."

**35:16** And Esau swore it — before God — that he would never harm Jacob as long as he lived.

**35:17** Rebekah called Jacob back in and gave him the news. Esau had reconciled. He had sworn an oath. She was filled with joy.

**35:18** Not long after, Rebekah got sick and died. Both Jacob and Esau were grief-stricken.

**35:19** They buried her in the cave at Machpelah near Mamre, beside her husband Isaac. All her sons and Jacob's sons carried her there with weeping and mourning.

**35:20** In the forty-sixth jubilee, first week, second year, Isaac died. Jacob and Esau buried him together.

**35:21** Esau went home to Edom. Jacob stayed in Hebron. Whenever Esau's family ran short, Jacob sent food.

**35:22** When Esau passed through the area, he sent Jacob gifts and good wishes. Between the two of them, peace lasted all their parents' lives.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Rebekah's testament is one of the most humanly moving passages in Jubilees. She functions here as a peace-broker who engineers what Genesis never achieves: a genuine reconciliation between Jacob and Esau, secured by oath. Her declaration of love for Jacob (v.7) is especially striking given the scheming role she played in earlier chapters.*
